name: Indian destination weddings
short: Three or four days of celebration, with your families flown in and looked after from the moment they land.
summary: Mehndi by the pool, a sangeet in a colonial mansion, pheras on the sand at Bentota. A short flight from home, and every guest looked after from arrival to farewell.

image.alt: The Temple of the Tooth lit up across the lake in Kandy at dusk

intro.heading: Close enough for every aunt. Far enough to feel like an occasion.
paragraphs: Sri Lanka is a short direct flight from India's major cities, with food your families will recognise and settings they will not have seen before: beaches with no crowds on them, colonial mansions, temples lit at night.
We are the team on the ground. We move the guests, hold the rooms, find the venues and keep each day to time, working beside your wedding planner or with suppliers we trust if you do not have one.

schedule.heading: How the days usually run.
schedule.lede: A shape most of our families start from, then change. Every event can move venue, swap order or drop out.

items.title: Welcome dinner
items.body: Guests arrive through the day and are met at the airport. The evening is a relaxed dinner on the lawn, so everyone settles before the ceremonies begin.

items.title: Mehndi and haldi
items.body: By the pool or in a garden pavilion, with shade, music and a menu that runs from breakfast into lunch.

items.title: Sangeet
items.body: The big night: a colonial mansion or a hotel ballroom, staging and sound, and performers if your family is not bringing its own.

items.title: Pheras on the beach
items.body: A mandap on the sand at sunset, a priest who knows your traditions, and Jain or sattvic menus where you need them.

items.title: Reception
items.body: Dinner and dancing for the whole party, with transport back to every hotel on a timetable.

items.title: Farewell, or a few more days
items.body: Departures timed to the flights, or a short journey for guests who want to see the hill country or the south coast.

includes.heading: What we take off your family's plate.
includes.body: One team in Sri Lanka for everything that happens after the invitations go out. Your planner leads the look; we make it run.

items.title: Guest travel
items.body: Flight advice, airport welcome desks, coaches timed to arrivals, and a room list we keep up to date as RSVPs change.

items.title: Hotels and venues
items.body: Room blocks across one or several hotels, venue sourcing and site visits, and the permits a beach ceremony needs.

items.title: Food your families eat
items.body: Menus agreed with the hotel chefs, including Jain, sattvic, vegetarian and halal, with tastings before the day.

items.title: Suppliers and staging
items.body: Décor, florists, lighting, sound, photographers, dhol players and Kandyan drummers, booked and briefed.

items.title: Guest days out
items.body: Tea country, a safari morning or a temple visit for guests who arrive early or stay on.

questions.q: Can you work with our wedding planner in India?
questions.a: Yes, and most of our families do. The planner leads the design and the guest experience; we handle everything on the ground in Sri Lanka and report to them.

questions.q: How many guests can you host?
questions.a: We plan weddings from about 80 guests to several hundred. Above 250 the choice of hotels narrows, so we start with the venue and build the guest plan around it.

questions.q: Can you arrange Jain or sattvic food?
questions.a: Yes. We agree menus with the hotel kitchens well ahead, and a tasting before the wedding makes sure the food is right.
November to April is dry on the west and south coasts, which suits beach ceremonies. From May to September we look at the hill country or the east coast instead.
